name: Hezekiah
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Ahaz sleeps with his fathers and Hezekiah his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Hezekiah son of Ahaz begins to reign over Judah in the third year of Hoshea, the last king of Israel before the captivity.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: In Hezekiah's fourth year Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, and after three years, in Hezekiah's sixth year, Samaria is taken.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Hezekiah sends to Lakish acknowledging offense and agrees to bear whatever tribute is laid on him.
Assyria appoints three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold, so Hezekiah gives all the silver of the house of the Most High and even cuts the gold from the temple doors.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: The first example of the punishment of the proud: the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh with a great host against Jerusalem, taunting king Hezekiah: what confidence is this wherein thou trustest? He mocked their trust in Egypt, a bruised reed, and mocked their trust in the Lord, and even claimed, the Lord said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: He argues that because Hezekiah removed the high places, even Judah's own worship is now confined to one altar, twisting the reform into a weakness.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Assyria was a rising empire conquering the nations around us. They destroyed the northern kingdom, then came against the southern kingdom during Hezekiah's reign. Hezekiah was a righteous king, so the Lord had his back, but Judah was very fearful.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: He offered two thousand horses if they would give up, and threatened them with siege conditions in the crudest terms, and called out in the Jews' language so all the people on the wall could hear: let not Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord, saying, The Lord will surely deliver us. It is the same thing they try with us now: things get bad and the enemy says, you think your God is going to come and deliver you?

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Rabshakeh cries aloud in the Jews' language, warning the people not to let Hezekiah deceive them or make them trust in the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Rabshakeh refused, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews' language so everyone would hear: let not Hezekiah deceive you; neither let Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord, saying, the Lord will surely deliver us. Make an agreement with me, eat every man of his own vine, until I come and take you away to a land like your own land. Pay your tribute, and then I will deport you all out of your land and put our own people in it.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and tell him the words of Rabshakeh.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: When King Hezekiah heard it, he rent his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord, and sent to Isaiah the prophet: this day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and blasphemy. What was the blasphemy? Rabshakeh saying, your God will not deliver you; the gods of the nations are nothing. The king of Assyria sent him to reproach the living God.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: When king Hezekiah heard it, he rent his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord, and sent to Isaiah the prophet. A government always had spiritual advisers; the king got threatened and said, go get Isaiah. When the nation of Israel is threatened, you get the man of God.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: When Hezekiah hears the reproach of Assyria he rends his clothes, covers himself with sackcloth, and goes into the house of the Most High, then sends his servants to Isaiah the prophet.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

points: Hearing that Tirhakah king of Ethiopia has come out to fight against him, Sennacherib sends messengers again to Hezekiah with a threatening letter.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

points: Rabshakeh had cried in the Jews' language: let not Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord; make an agreement with me by a present and I will carry you to a land like your own; which of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of my hand? The people held their peace at the king's commandment.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

points: Hezekiah receives the letter, reads it, goes up to the house of the Most High, and spreads it before Him.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

points: Assyria took the northern kingdom around 722 BC and came for Judah around 701. Hezekiah received the letter of threats, went up to the house of the Lord, spread it before him, and prayed: thou alone art God of all the kingdoms, the nations' gods were wood and stone, save us that all the earth may know thou art the Lord. Cast all your care upon him, 1 Peter 5:7.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

points: The prayer of Hezekiah is that the Most High show His power and prove His people are the chosen and that He is the one true living God. This is a righteous prayer, the same praying for the downfall of enemies and for righteous judgment to come upon them.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

points: Hezekiah falls sick unto death, and Isaiah brings the word to set his house in order, for he shall die and not live.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Hezekiah turns his face to the wall and prays, asking the Most High to remember how he walked before Him in truth and with a perfect heart, and he weeps sore.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Hezekiah asks for a sign that the Most High will heal him and that he shall go up to the house of the Most High on the third day.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Isaiah offers the shadow going forward ten degrees or back ten degrees, and Hezekiah answers that going forward is a light thing, but let it return backward ten degrees.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Berodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sends letters and a present to Hezekiah, having heard he had been sick; this is the introduction of Babylon, still only a province under Assyria at this time.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Hezekiah hearkens to them and shows them all his precious things, his silver, gold, spices, ointment, and armor, holding nothing back, trusting his enemies because of the gift.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Isaiah asks what the men saw and where they came from, then declares that all in the house shall be carried into Babylon, and Hezekiah's own sons shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in Isaiah 39.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: The rest of the acts of Hezekiah, including how he made a pool and a conduit and brought water into the city, are written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Hezekiah was one of the very few righteous kings, so righteous that the Most High extended his life, and Manasseh his son reigned in his stead.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Hezekiah sleeps with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Manasseh did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, after the abominations of the heathen. He built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed, reared up altars for Baal, worshiped all the host of heaven, built altars in the house of the Lord, made his son pass through the fire, observed times, used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards. He went back and served the same gods and altars his father destroyed.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: Manasseh began at twelve and reigned fifty-five years, and did not follow his father's example: he rebuilt the high places Hezekiah had cast down, reared altars to Baal and a grove as Ahab did, and worshipped the host of heaven, the stars and the zodiac.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: He rebuilds the high places Hezekiah destroyed, rears altars for Baal, makes a grove as Ahab did, and worships the host of heaven, even building altars in the house of the Most High where He set His name; this is a wickedness with zero fear of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: The record runs through Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah, keeping the royal succession by name.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: Ahaz slept with his fathers and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but not in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead. The Most High is the only one who can bring the people out of their condition, then and now.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

points: Hezekiah wrote to Ephraim and Manasseh, from Beersheba to Dan, to keep the Passover at Jerusalem. Many laughed the letters to scorn, but some of Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Now that the temple is cleansed and the priests sanctified, Hezekiah sends letters to all Israel and Judah, even to Ephraim and Manasseh, calling them to keep the Passover at Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

points: Hezekiah prayed, the good Lord pardon every one that prepareth his heart to seek God, though he be not cleansed. The Lord hearkened and healed the people, and this is the pattern behind Acts 10.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun eat the Passover otherwise than it was written, but Hezekiah prays that the good Lord pardon everyone who prepares his heart to seek God, and the Lord hearkens and heals the people. Grace and mercy are present here in the Old Testament.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

points: Hezekiah and the princes give thousands of bullocks and sheep, and all the congregation, the priests, the Levites, and the strangers out of Israel rejoice together.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

points: Hezekiah appoints the priests and Levites to their courses for burnt offerings, peace offerings, and thanksgiving, and sets the king's portion for the daily, Sabbath, new moon, and feast offerings as written in the law.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 31: The Tithe Restored

points: They lay the tithe in heaps from the third to the seventh month, and when Hezekiah and the princes see the heaps they bless the Lord and his people Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 31: The Tithe Restored

points: Hezekiah does throughout all Judah that which is good and right and true before the Lord his God.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 31: The Tithe Restored

points: Sennacherib sends servants to Jerusalem asking on what the people trust that they abide in the siege, and claims Hezekiah is persuading them to die by famine and thirst.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: He mocks that Hezekiah took away the high places and altars and commanded worship at one altar, twisting obedience to the commandment into a weakness.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: He argues that no god of any nation delivered its people from his hand, so neither will the God of Hezekiah. This is the same seed the world plants to make Israel weary and turn a people off one accord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: Sennacherib's servants speak yet more against the Lord God and against his servant Hezekiah, and he writes letters to rail on the Lord God of Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amos, pray and cry to heaven over this railing.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: Thus the Lord saves Hezekiah and Jerusalem and guides them on every side, and many bring gifts to the Lord and presents to Hezekiah, so he is magnified in the sight of all nations, a picture of the gifts the nations will bring back to Israel in the kingdom.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: In those days Hezekiah is sick to death, prays to the Lord, and is given a sign.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: But Hezekiah renders not according to the benefit done to him, for his heart is lifted up in pride, and wrath comes upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem. When things go well, do not get puffed up and make it about yourself.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: Then Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord does not come upon them in his days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: Hezekiah has exceeding riches and honour, making treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, and spices, and storehouses for corn, wine, oil, and cattle, for God gives him very much substance.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: All Judah honoured Hezekiah at his death and buried him in the chiefest of the sepulchres of the sons of David, and Manasseh reigned in his stead.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: When the ambassadors of Babylon come to inquire of the wonder, God leaves him to try him and know his heart. Hezekiah then sleeps with his fathers, is buried in honour among the sons of David, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: He rebuilds the high places his father Hezekiah had broken down, rears up altars for Baal, makes groves, and worships all the host of heaven and serves them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: These are also proverbs of Solomon copied out by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah. Hezekiah and his men studied Solomon's writings because they understood that what was written before their time was written for our learning, to seek out the ways of our fathers and find the right paths.
Go back and read about King Hezekiah in the prophets, Chronicles, and Kings as a homework assignment.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

points: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz concerns Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. These are the days in which Isaiah prophesied.

Isaiah was a servant and prophet during Hezekiah's reign, before the Assyrian captivity destroyed the nation. The split between the northern and southern kingdoms had already come, going back to Solomon's idolatry and the friction between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: Sennacherib king of Assyria took Judah's defenced cities and sent Rabshakeh to mock Hezekiah in the Jews' language, boasting that no god of any nation had delivered his land out of the king of Assyria's hand.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

points: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defended cities of Judah and took them. Assyria was the rod the Most High used to press Judah.

note.label: Isaiah 36: Rabshakeh's Blasphemy Against Jerusalem

points: He twists Hezekiah's removal of the high places, claiming it offended the Most High, and boasts that even Assyria was sent by the Lord to destroy the land. He speaks as though the Most High is on his side.

note.label: Isaiah 36: Rabshakeh's Blasphemy Against Jerusalem

points: He tells them not to let Hezekiah make them trust in the Most High to deliver the city, but to make an agreement with him and come out, promising each man his own vine and fig tree until he takes them to a land like their own. It is a bribe dressed up as mercy.

note.label: Isaiah 36: Rabshakeh's Blasphemy Against Jerusalem

points: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and tell him the words of Rabshakeh. They bring the blasphemy before the king in mourning.

note.label: Isaiah 36: Rabshakeh's Blasphemy Against Jerusalem

points: When Hezekiah hears the words, he rends his clothes, covers himself with sackcloth, and goes into the house of the Most High. He turns to the Most High rather than to Egypt or to fear.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Sennacherib sends messengers again to Hezekiah, telling him not to let the God in whom he trusts deceive him that Jerusalem will not be given into his hand. He renews the same threat and mockery.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Hezekiah receives the letter, reads it, goes up to the house of the Most High, and spreads it before Him. He lays the whole threat out before the Most High in prayer.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: In those days Hezekiah was sick unto death, and Isaiah the son of Amoz came and told him to set his house in order, for he would die and not live. Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed, reminding the Most High how he had walked before him in truth and with a perfect heart, and he wept sore.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: The word of the Lord came again to Isaiah: the Most High had heard the prayer and seen the tears, and would add fifteen years to Hezekiah's days and deliver the city out of the hand of the king of Assyria.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: This is the writing of Hezekiah after he had been sick and recovered. He speaks of being deprived of the residue of his years, going to the gates of the grave, his life cut off like a weaver cuts the thread.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, having heard he had been sick and recovered. Hezekiah was glad of them and showed them all the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, the ointment, and all his armor, holding nothing back in all his dominion.

note.label: Isaiah 39: The Treasures Shown and Babylon Foretold

points: Isaiah came and asked what the men had said and where they came from. When Hezekiah answered that they came from Babylon and had seen everything among his treasures, Isaiah declared the days would come when all in his house, and what his fathers had stored up, would be carried to Babylon with nothing left.

note.label: Isaiah 39: The Treasures Shown and Babylon Foretold

points: The prophecy adds that Hezekiah's own sons that issue from him would be taken and made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah called the word of the Lord good because there would be peace and truth in his days.

note.label: Isaiah 39: The Treasures Shown and Babylon Foretold

points: The elders rise and recall that Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah that Zion would be plowed like a field, yet Hezekiah did not put him to death but feared the Most High, who then repented of the evil.

note.label: Jeremiah 26: Jeremiah Threatened for Prophesying

points: The word of the Lord came unto Hosea the son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

note.label: Hosea 1: A Wife of Whoredoms and the Sand of the Sea

points: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

note.label: Micah 1: The Lord Cometh Forth Out of His Place

cases.name: Hezekiah
cases.charge: Trusting in the Lord God of Israel, so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah; cleaving to him and keeping his commandments; breaking the brasen serpent; opening the doors of the house of the Lord and keeping the passover
cases.preview: Hezekiah trusted in the Lord God of Israel so that no king of Judah before or after him was like him;

cases.name: Hezekiah and the ambassadors of Babylon
cases.charge: Rendering not again according to the benefit done unto him, for his heart was lifted up; shewing all his treasures to the men of Babylon
cases.preview: Healed of a mortal sickness, given fifteen years, and shown the shadow going back ten degrees, Hezekiah did not repay the benefit done to him, for his heart grew proud (2 Chronicles 32:24-25).
